description: Which goal documents are valid, and why not, as {field, code} errors. A valid document matches urn:awrad:goal-model:1#/$defs/goal_document and follows the goal rules the schema can't express (goal-model/v1 goal_validity). Structure is checked first: a missing member is `required`; an unknown member `not_allowed`; a wrong type, an unknown enum value, a session kind that doesn't exist, a non-UUID ID or an impossible month-day (31 April, on the range's start or end) `invalid`; an empty string `blank`; text over its limit (name and snapshot title 120 code points, snapshot Arabic 5,000) `too_long`; a list over its limit (100 versions, 500 pauses, 1,000 excused days) `too_many`; an empty list that needs an item (`versions`, `weekdays`, month `days`, `dates`, yearly `ranges`) `required` on that list's own pointer, while an empty `sessions` list is valid and means no sessions; repeated excused days `duplicate`; a snapshot title without any text `required` on the title. Only a structurally valid document is checked against the goal rules, reported as in contracts/sync/v1/README.md (Goal rules as field errors). Errors are sorted by field, then code; a `rejected` receipt reports the same errors with /document in front. Clients check before saving; the server checks every put.

document.description: Any JSON object; it may be invalid.
